steps.name: Elderly Infected
steps.text: (Sargonian) ...He went home, and left the world behind.

steps.name: Elderly Infected
steps.text: (Sargonian) Our hearts ache because fate is ever unjust.

steps.name: Elderly Infected
steps.text: (Sargonian) But we need not grieve. Because he is now free from the suffering of existence.

steps.name: Elderly Infected
steps.text: (Sargonian) We sing for him, as he has at last returned to the earth.

steps.name: Elderly Infected
steps.text: (Sargonian) His relatives, his loved ones, need not shed tears.

steps.name: Elderly Infected
steps.text: (Sargonian) Death is a mercy of our world. And we are the heirs to all things.

steps.name: Elderly Infected
steps.text: (Sargonian) ...May it all turn to dust.

steps.name: Elderly Infected
steps.text: (Sargonian) ...May it all return to the wild.

steps.name: Elderly Infected
steps.text: (Sargonian) ...To which we too will one day return.

a.text: A roughly polished stone monument adorned with a few lines carved into its uneven surface stands in the shadow of a dead tree.
'He was Infected. He was a Doctor.'

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Are you okay?

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: ...Hard to say.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I heard the old lizard man say that only important people get funerals in this country.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Most ordinary folks just die when they die, and their families bury them in the wastes. No tombstones, no mourning.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: The people who live on the huge platforms, the moving cities, have to cremate the dead and bury the ashes under those major roads, since space is so precious in the city.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Cemeteries are rare in an ordinary settlement, where a disaster can come through and wipe out any memory of where the dead are buried.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: There's basically no religion in Sargon. Most people here don't believe in an afterlife. They think the dead return to the earth, and become part of it.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Looking at it like that, it's a pretty honest and practical culture. I like it.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: So Miarow's grave will be lost someday?

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Probably. But we held a funeral for him. And that was important.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: I can't really accept that.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: After seeing what I saw, it's hard to accept how he went.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: We probably bear some responsibility, Alexsandr.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: If it weren't for Miarow, we would've had a much rougher time here.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: I've been thinking, what if we'd moved a little faster? If we were tougher? If we really decided to do something for those sick people?

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: If we...

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I don't think it's a good idea to get caught up in thoughts like that.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Miarow made his own choices. This isn't your fault.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: The big girl was trying to fulfill her duty. As an aristocrat growing up in this culture, in this system, her willingness to shelter the sick was definitely a noble act.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Judging by how the Rhodes Islanders talk, Miarow was very, very sick.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: For him, death was something that hung over him every day.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: It's a miracle he lasted as long as he did, in his condition.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: That's how they live. And there's not much we can do about it.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: But did we really do the right thing?

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: We were so sure that if we reached out to help them, we would actually be helping them.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: And I have no idea why.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: We lived with those sick people.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: But we didn't know anything about the Infected. We thought of that 'Oripathy' like a slightly infectious cancer, the deadly, incurable disease we already knew.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: But this isn't a disease, really... it's a disaster.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: We don't know anything about it. And we still tried to save them.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: You can't blame yourself for nothing, Cohen.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: It's pointless.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I understand what you're feeling.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: But you can't deny what we did.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Remember when I was up on that roof with nothing to do? I had all that time on my hands.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I sat there, watching Miarow's clinic, watching the people who lived there.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: As a visitor from another world, I witnessed this one.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I'm not a sharp person, but even I could see the many, terrible, cruel things.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: One night, one of the townsfolk was carrying a package from another's house under the cover of darkness.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: It was a burlap-wrapped parcel, about as tall as a man.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I watched them load the package into a handcart and make their way along the edge of town to the rocky desert, disappearing behind the boulders on the south side.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I saw it happen just like that several times. Maybe twice in the past three weeks. And it must have been happening in other places too, where I couldn't see it.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: You never mentioned this before.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I didn't want to say anything. I didn't have a reason to.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: You're right. We're outsiders. We're not from this country. We're not even from this world.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: We can't understand the people here. Their history, their culture, their lives, their feelings, we couldn't hope to know.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: And I have no right to point my finger at something I don't understand. There's a reason they do what they do.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: That's how it should be.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: But then, one night, my curiosity got the better of me. I followed the path to the boulder where they buried the sack.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I saw the light shimmering beneath the sand. I saw the dust rising up from the rocks and dissipating into the air.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: That dust is so bright, in the dark of the night.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I knew, of course, what was in the sack. I could probably guess what the dust was.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: And naturally, we all know exactly what it is now.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: There was an old woman who sat by the door of the house where the sack came from. After that night, I never saw her again.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Kötz spent every day with the townsfolk. He must've known about it too.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: What was the excuse you made up before...? Everyone looks like they've had chemical warfare training? They know to cover their noses and mouths? What a lame explanation.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Because I'd seen the reason.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: You just asked me if we really did the right thing.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: The answer is simple: we helped them. Because that's what our morals, our conscience, told us to do.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Aging, illness, and death are inevitable. In this world and ours.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Even if there wasn't this Oripathy, the people wouldn't suffer any less.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Even without the disease, they'd have war, taxation, and natural disasters crushing the poor.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: See their Lord and this town, what kind of a society do they live in?

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Such feudalism would be far behind the times in the history of the Earth we know. But it's the reality for them.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: By our standards, they're not living in a civilized world.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I've seen enough *profanity* over the years, Cohen. You know what I mean.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: This world sucks. But there's still something we can do about it.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Don't turn your back on our good work. Morality and conscience aren't wrong.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: ...*Sigh*.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: You're right, Alexsandr.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: Forget I said anything. I'm just too tired.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: It's been too long since you got a good night's sleep.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: We're all tired.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Someone's coming.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: I don't know what to say. This is all on me.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: Because I was stupid and impulsive.

a.text: The tall Reproba holds a golden seal. She grips it tightly, infusing it with her own conviction.
The seal melts and falls from her hand, spilling onto the roughly polished stone tablet.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: Originium Arts...

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: That was a medal of honor given to my father by the Lord Ameer. He was one of the Ameer's strongest warriors, and the town of Long Spring was a reward for his service.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: My father was strong, kind, just.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: He always was, ever since I was small.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: The Tulla family was built on the blood and bones of miners.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: For years, my father grew wealthy digging Originium out of the ground.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: But with it came the spread of Oripathy. It was just the miners, at first... but it eventually spread through the town.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: When the Originium closer to the surface was all mined out, my father closed the quarry. He wouldn't let anyone dig any deeper.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: He created the Infected quarter, and sent men to protect the people living there. He couldn't just sit on the pile of Infected corpses and count his gold.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: He always hoped my brother Drudge and I could do better.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: I don't know what happened to Drudge while he was studying in Columbia. I just saw him turn more and more evil.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: It wasn't until my father kicked him out of the house that I realized the man was no longer my brother.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: But I disappointed Father too.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: I'm not a worthy successor to his achievements, or his legacy.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: I'm unworthy.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: I did nothing. I couldn't protect Long Spring. I couldn't protect my father's people. I couldn't even kill Drudge. I let him get away.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Drudge's supporters, what kind of people are they?

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: I don't know them well. All I know is that they are from a Columbian organization called Volvort Kochinski.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: It wasn't the first time I dealt with those Columbians...

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: They're wicked and greedy. All they care about is how to dig more rocks out from under the town. They don't give a thought to the people living in it.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Sounds familiar.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: My father used to say that if I just became a warrior, I could protect my home with strength alone.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: A warrior can defeat another warrior. But violence isn't a solution to true evil.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: ...I never understood what he was referring to with 'true evil'.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: I always thought Drudge had turned evil.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: ...But now I know Drudge was just a tiny little sliver of evil. And it was still enough to beat me.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: There are times when a fight to the death can't solve the problem.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: What are you going to do next?

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: I don't know. Drudge ran off, and his mercenaries fell apart.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: But he left behind those monsters. Long Spring isn't really habitable anymore...

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: For the time being, at least, I have to protect my home. That's where the town's survivors are.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: How many people can your home house?

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: ......There's a shelter in the basement of the manor. It can hold a lot of people, but we don't have enough food and water.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: Sorry, I shouldn't be complaining to you about these things.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: I actually came to thank you for protecting the people of Long Spring through all this.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: No thanks necessary.

steps.name: Picale
steps.text: I... I have something I must do. Excuse me.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: She's a good person. It's hard to believe that evil *profanity* is her brother.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Here you are, Miss Cohen.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Did I come at a bad time?

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: Oh, no. We were just about to leave.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: The Infected gave this to me. It's Dr. Miarow's... estate. In the box.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: After talking it over with the Infected, they decided it would be best to give them to you.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Open it.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: Is that proper?

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Of course. He was our friend.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: What's inside?

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: A map. And a book.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: It's a Sargonian version of 'The Traveler's Guide to Urban Columbia'.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: As for the map... It looks kind of old. Let's see here...

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Oh... This area should be Tkaronto. It's a Columbia border city. I've been there before.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: And is this stack here money?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Columbian gold certificates... Dr. Miarow actually had some savings.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: I remember he said he would leave here someday and go to a place called Columbia.

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: 'To become a real doctor.'

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: Short as his time was, he still had a plan for his life.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Hold on. There's a note here. Let me see.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: What does it say?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: ...Should I read it?

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: 'If you're reading this note, thank you for helping me deal with this stuff.'

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: 'Give the money to someone. I definitely don't need it anymore.'

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: 'Don't lose the box. It was my mother's.'

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: 'Although I don't know who you are, my friend,'

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: 'I still hope your life turns out okay.'

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: '—— Miarow '

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: ...I don't know how to express myself here... What can I do or say in the face of his legacy?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Dr. Miarow was a strong man.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Dreams are a luxury for the Infected. They're like precious, fragile gemstones.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Even in Columbia, the Infected are zoned to certain areas of the city. Most people live their whole lives struggling to get out of them.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: The vast majority of the time, contracting Oripathy is a death sentence... if a deferred one.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Reality forces you to give up on your dreams, your lifestyle, and ultimately life itself.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: It's hard for anyone to be hopeful about life in the face of cruel reality.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: What on earth was supporting him?

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: Someone like Miarow should not have lived like this. He shouldn't have died like this.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: Wait, where are you going?

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: To find the big girl.

steps.name: Ash
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Tachanka
steps.text: I want to talk to her. I have a plan.
